objective: Help learners and study-tool builders keep one review history when a chapter, lecture transcript, or later upload repeats the same fact.

source_need.problem: A later lecture-transcript upload can generate cards already created from an earlier chapter upload, because upload-local comparison cannot see the established collection.
source_need.policy: The issue is evidence of a real need, not a promotion surface. No issue reply, mention, or project pitch was made.

conversion_path.offer: Fixed USD 250 for one rights-cleared collection on one existing machine, up to 12 source units and 20 test questions, with up to two cited browser cards when usable and a clear go/no-go recommendation.
conversion_path.live_review: The English, Japanese, and Traditional Chinese editions each returned HTTP 200 with the reviewed offer and one direct fit-check link.

lazyblog.policy: The article solves the design problem before mentioning any owned work. It cites three public repositories only as architectural patterns and explicitly says none is a finished cross-upload deduplicator.

x.content: Duplicate cards can be a data-model problem: a chapter and lecture repeat one fact, but each import creates a new note. Keep one fact, attach both source spans, and update the same Anki note. Design: blog.lazying.art/?p=3782&utm_source=x&utm_campaign=card_dedup

reddit.title: One fact, two sources: avoiding duplicate study cards
reddit.content:
One repeated fact should not become two review histories.

If a textbook chapter and a lecture transcript teach the same thing, keep each source’s original wording, but attach both citations to one accepted note. Exact keys catch retries and formatting changes. Fuzzy matching should only flag likely paraphrases for review.

I wrote out the SQLite schema, update rules, and test cases here:
https://blog.lazying.art/?p=3782&utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=profile&utm_campaign=card_dedup

I maintain the guide.
reddit.policy: First-party profile resource only. It is not a generated reply in a community thread. The closing line gives a concise maintainer disclosure without interrupting the useful explanation.

instagram.policy: Do not turn a database design article into a generic graphic. Wait for a real, rights-cleared before-and-after study artifact.

hackernews.policy: Do not post agent-authored comments or submit the article without an independently relevant discussion.

limits: The public repositories demonstrate source, hierarchy, and knowledge-identity patterns; they do not implement the complete deduplication workflow described in the article.
Fuzzy similarity creates review candidates only until labeled tests support a safer decision boundary.
No public issue reply, direct message, automated community comment, or customer claim was created.
